questions.q: What does "identity is the new perimeter" mean in a cloud and remote-work world?
options: Network firewalls are now more important than ever before
Identity verification has replaced the need for encryption entirely
Only on-premises users need to be authenticated
Strong identity verification, not network location, is what actually gates access to resources
questions.explain: With no network edge left to defend, who is making the request — proven through strong identity verification — is what actually decides access.

questions.q: Why did IAM and MFA become the real front line of defense in this model?
options: Because firewalls are no longer manufactured
Because cloud providers no longer support network security groups
Because correct credentials alone are often enough to reach a cloud resource directly, with no network layer left behind to catch a mistake
Because IAM and MFA replace the need for Zero Trust principles
questions.explain: In an identity-perimeter world, the sign-in itself is usually the primary defense — which is why IAM and MFA carry the weight the firewall used to carry.

questions.q: How does the castle-and-moat firewall's role differ from identity's role as the new perimeter?
options: The firewall verified identity directly, which is unchanged today
The firewall was the primary defense with internal protections behind it; identity is now often the primary defense with no network layer behind it
Identity only matters for on-premises resources, not cloud ones
There is no difference — both serve the exact same function
questions.explain: A compromised firewall used to still face internal protections; a compromised identity in a cloud/remote-work setup often faces no network layer at all.

questions.q: In the SaaS HR system example, what is the only thing standing between an outsider and payroll data?
options: The sign-in page — who the person is, how strongly they proved it, and whether their role warrants access
A corporate VPN connection
The company's on-premises firewall
A physical badge reader at the office
questions.explain: The SaaS app has no network boundary to be inside of — identity verification at sign-in is the only real gate.

questions.q: How does "identity as the perimeter" connect to the Zero Trust tenet of least privilege access?
options: Least privilege access only applies to network traffic, not identities
A verified identity should only be handed the specific permissions its role requires, not broad standing access
It means identity verification can be skipped once least privilege is configured
Least privilege access means giving every verified identity full administrative rights
questions.explain: Even after identity is verified, least privilege access limits what that identity can actually do — it isn't a blanket pass.
